system.name: Oasis
system.one_liner: a system that pools PCIe devices such as NICs and SSDs across hosts in software over CXL memory pools

components.name: Pod-Wide Allocator
components.role: the Oasis control plane that maps PCIe devices to instances within a pod and manages load balancing and failover

components.name: Logical SSD Pool
components.role: tracks free, allocated, and failed SSDs available to the pod

components.name: Logical NIC Pool
components.role: tracks free, allocated, and failed NICs available to the pod

components.name: Instance
components.role: a compute instance that the allocator maps to specific SSD/NIC devices via instance-to-device mapping

components.name: Host 1
components.role: a host running an instance and engine connected to a pooled device

components.name: Host N
components.role: another host, illustrating that the same control path scales to N hosts

components.name: Engine
components.role: the per-device-class Oasis engine on a host that connects the local instance to the pooled device

flows.what: instance-to-device mapping allocating an SSD to the instance
instance-to-device mapping allocating a NIC to the instance
control path managing device assignment, load balancing, and failover

content.key_idea: A single pod-wide allocator tracks free, allocated, and failed SSDs and NICs and maps them to instances across many hosts, centralizing load balancing and failover.
content.reading_order: Top-down: the allocator's SSD and NIC pools feed an instance-to-device mapping, whose control path then reaches down to each host's instance and engine.

evidence: The Oasis control plane, which we call the pod-wide allo- cator, is responsible for mapping PCIe devices to instances
The allocator tracks the usage of each device and assigns resources to newly created instances
It can also dynamically migrate instances to other devices for load balancing or failover

summary: Figure 5 shows the pod-wide allocator, the control-plane component of Oasis that pools PCIe devices such as SSDs and NICs over CXL. Inside the allocator, a Logical SSD Pool and a Logical NIC Pool each track devices as Free, Allocated, or Failed; an Instance-to-Dev Mapping step assigns pooled devices to a requesting Instance. The allocator then exercises a Control Path down to each host in the pod, Host 1 through Host N, where a local Instance and Engine actually use the assigned SSD or NIC. The accompanying text explains that the allocator also tracks device usage, assigns resources to new instances, and can migrate instances between devices for load balancing or failover, applying both static policies (e.g., instance types) and dynamic policies (e.g., prioritizing instances under load).

notes: layout-proposal: pool-allocator hub over replica hosts — the hub itself contains its own two-pool sub-diagram (Logical SSD/NIC pools, Instance-to-Dev Mapping) before its Control Path fans out to N structurally identical hosts drawn in a row, a looser fit than a simple radial hub-spoke.
